appraisal_events.evidence: His clumsy apology only aggravates his offense; he swears extravagant oaths of love and sobs to both the narrator and Saint-Loup while having badmouthed each to the other; the narrator states plainly he did not believe any of it ('des paroles que je sentais inventées à l'instant même', 'pour la volupté hystérique de mentir'), and generalizes Bloch's manner as a kind of fraud that mixes truth with falsifying lies.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator systematically exposes Bloch's insincerity: his overwrought apologies, tears, and oaths of devotion to two people he has simultaneously slandered to each other are framed as hollow performance rather than genuine feeling, locally lowering him in the narrator's and reader's estimation.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch is portrayed as insincere and manipulative, badmouthing both the narrator and Saint-Loup to each other while performing exaggerated tenderness toward both, and the narrator explicitly disbelieves his protestations.
His theatrical oaths, sobs, and declarations are shown to carry no real weight ('n'ajoutait pas un grand poids'), undercutting the authority and credibility of his own speech.
